entry.title: Coding agents: ohmyjev's pi and omp adapters added as a counted row (on every Jev failure the gate returns without blocking, so the tool runs). 27 integrations read in source; 14 act on Jev's answer (3 fail-closed, 9 fallback, 2 fail-open), 10 do not, 3 are not settled (Hoppin-Sorter/jev-router, auto-mode 3.0.0, jcode). 13 new leads classed.

When Jev fails: ohmyjev's row names its pi and omp adapters, read at the same commit with the same five failure terms; still 80 implementations and no count changed. One file reference in its bypass cell corrected.

Alternatives: the Drex row quotes Nace.AI's website Terms and Privacy Policy (9 Oct; training by default with an opt-out, up to 30 days) next to its Console Service Terms and Data Processing Addendum (19 Oct; no training unless you opt in, deletion within 48 hours or 7 days); which controls is not stated. drex-v1.5's two prices shown in their own units.

Versions and aliases: Cloudflare's AI model catalog lists typesafe/jev-1.14.0 through AI Gateway (first seen by this catalogue on 21 Oct 2026; it may have been listed earlier; not tested). Aliases unchanged: jev-latest still gives jev-1.13.0.
New research report: coding agents on pi and omp, auto-mode and jcode, and Nace.AI's two sets of terms (21 Oct 2026).

Access status rechecked 21 Oct 2026, 05:11 UTC: signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price, rate-limit wording and model aliases unchanged (jev-latest still on jev-1.13.0; TypeSafe has published no date for the move to 1.14). Home now shows two notices: the Jev 1.14 preview and experimental-features notices came off after seven days; both facts stay on versions and aliases and limitations.

When Jev fails: new self-check. Pick what your code does in five failure conditions and see how many of the 80 implementations on the map made the same choice, with examples; same counts as the map (recomputed 19 Oct); it does not read or test code.
When Jev fails: checklist question 9 asks whether your code logs or shows when it falls back or fails open; not counted, because the map does not record it. Copyable checklist updated.

Corrected: current sentences on 14 pages that still gave the earlier count of 79 implementations, or its category numbers, now give 80 (for example, 10 let the action through on a Jev error; 19 of 80 let it go ahead).

Alternatives: Drex (Nace.AI) added as a hosted decision API with open weights; price and data terms quoted from Nace.AI's pages; claims against Jev are the vendor's own; 38 substitutes, 8 hosted APIs from other providers.

Rechecked: LiteLLM 1.106.0 keeps the Jev classifier's failure path; n8n 2.44.3 refuses to activate a workflow whose node lacks a required credential; OpenAI's Decisions API guide now accepts image URLs (no comparison-card cell changed).
New dated report: failure self-check, checklist question 9, and Drex on alternatives (20 Oct 2026).

Access status rechecked 20 Oct 2026, 05:13 UTC: signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price, rate-limit wording and model aliases unchanged (jev-latest still on jev-1.13.0; TypeSafe has published no date for the move to 1.14). Home keeps its four notices; none retired.

Access status rechecked 19 Oct 2026, 05:22 UTC: signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price, rate-limit wording and model aliases unchanged (jev-latest still on jev-1.13.0; TypeSafe has published no date for the move to 1.14). Home keeps its four notices; none retired.

When Jev fails: ohmyjev (a Claude Code module with Bash, Write/Edit and exfiltration gates) joins the checklist after its pi and omp adapters were read in full, so it counts 80 implementations with every failure cell recorded. On a Jev error 40 stop or hold the action, 22 fall back, 10 let it through, 5 return no decision and 3 are advisory; the action goes ahead in 19 of 80.

Claude Code and MCP: ohmyjev's bypass cell is recorded and it is counted on the failure checklist; the short answer over ten guardrails is unchanged. jkudish/jev-mcp rows now cite the commit their cells were read at (53fe575, 0.11.0), with the 0.13.0 and 0.14.1 checks listed separately (also on products).

Alternatives: Liquid AI d1-ultra, Mouse-1 (preview) and Eevo (Upright) added as hosted decision APIs from other providers, with status, published prices and data terms quoted from their own pages; 37 substitutes, 7 of them hosted APIs. Their claims against Jev are the vendors' own; no graded comparison.
Content moderation (11 cells) and support-ticket triage (9 cells): failure cells now lead with the failure checklist's terms, with the detail on the line below. No outcome changed.

Products: beside the VentureBeat-relayed Vercel adoption claim, Vercel's own AI Gateway production-index figures (35.3% of paid AI Gateway teams in Jev's first two weeks; 0.27% of gateway spend over that period). Reported; Vercel sells gateway access to Jev.
New dated report: the failure map completed with ohmyjev, the jev-mcp commits, and what Liquid AI d1-ultra, Mouse-1 and Eevo publish about prices and data terms.
